violations.why: closer1_isr (prio 5) can preempt writer1_isr between its write and read, so the read sees 1 instead of 0.
closer1_isr can preempt between the two reads in writer1_isr, so they can return different values.
closer1_isr can overwrite the value between writer1's write and its later read.
closer2_isr (prio 3) can preempt closer4_isr (prio 1) between its two writes and read an intermediate state.
The ++ in writer2_isr is a non-atomic read-modify-write. writer4_isr (prio 4) can preempt it, and its write of 10 is then lost.
writer4_isr (prio 4) can preempt closer2_isr after it sets 42, so the check at 1038 sees 0.
closer1_isr (prio 5) can preempt closer2_isr between its write and its check and change the value (it ends by setting 0).
writer4_isr can preempt closer2_isr between its check and its final write, so the check result is stale.
writer3_isr and the higher-priority ISRs can preempt closer3_isr and clobber expect_close before its check.
writer4_isr can preempt closer2_isr between setting count=1 and testing it, so the test sees 0.
writer3_isr (prio 3) can preempt closer3_isr (prio 2) between its write and its read of count.
closer1_isr can preempt writer1_isr between count=0 and the test, so the test sees 1.
